function.name: calculate_mortgage_payment
function.description: Calculate the monthly mortgage payment given the loan amount, annual interest rate, and number of years. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

loan_amount.description: The loan amount. This is a float type value.

annual_rate.description: The annual interest rate in percentage. This is a float type value.

years.description: Number of years the mortgage is amortized over.

message.content:
I’m sorry, but I don’t have access to live market data, so I can’t tell you the exact current mortgage or lending rate at this moment.

Mortgage rates fluctuate constantly based on economic conditions, central‑bank policy, credit‑worthiness, loan type, term, and lender pricing. If you’re looking for the most up‑to‑date figure, here are a few reliable ways to get it:

| Source | How to Check | Typical Frequency |
|--------|--------------|-------------------|
| **Federal Reserve (U.S.)** – “Effective Federal Funds Rate” | https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy.htm | Daily updates |
| **Bank of England** – “Bank Rate” | https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy | Daily updates |
| **European Central Bank** – “Eurozone Main Refinancing Operations Rate” | https://www.ecb.europa.eu/stats/policy_and_exchange_rates/html/index.en.html | Daily updates |
| **Commercial Lenders / Mortgage Brokers** | Visit their websites or call; many publish “current average rates” | Updated weekly or daily |
| **Financial News Sites** – Bloomberg, Reuters, CNBC | Search “mortgage rates” | Updated throughout the day |

If you’re specifically interested in U.S. mortgage rates, the *average* 30‑year fixed‑rate mortgage has hovered around 7–8 % in recent months, but individual offers can range from roughly 5 % for highly rated borrowers to 9 %+ for riskier profiles. In the UK, the Bank of England’s base rate sits near 5 %, and typical 25‑year mortgages are quoted around 6–7 %. In the Eurozone, the ECB’s main refinancing rate is about 4 %, and mortgage rates tend to be 1–2 percentage points higher.

For the most accurate and personalized quote, contact a lender directly or use an online comparison tool that pulls real‑time data from multiple banks.
